s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual field defect with worsening headaches and a history of intracerebral hemorrhage
salient_findings: Left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage on noncontrast head CT
Left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage on contrast-enhanced brain MRI
key_facts: 36-year-old Asian man
4-month history of worsening headaches
Complete right homonymous hemianopia
History of left occipital intracerebral hematoma of unknown cause 2 years earlier
Normal vital signs
Neurologic testing confirmed visual field defect without other focal deficits
Left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage on noncontrast head CT
Left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage on contrast-enhanced brain MRI
Subtotal removal of the mass during left occipital craniotomy
Intraoperative finding of the mass invading the falx cerebri and adjacent cortex
Postoperative CT showed no complications

shortlist.label: Hemangiopericytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination demonstrated spindle cells forming masses with branching ectatic vasculature, focal collagenous regions, and up to 20 mitoses per ten high-power fields, consistent with Hemangiopericytoma

shortlist.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Immunohistochemical studies showed strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1, which can be seen in Solitary fibrous tumor

shortlist.label: Cavernous angioma
shortlist.why_kept: Contrast-enhanced brain MRI revealed a left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage, suggesting a cavernous angioma

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Intraoperative finding of the mass invading the falx cerebri and adjacent cortex, which can be seen in Meningioma

shortlist.label: Arteriovenous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: History of left occipital intracerebral hematoma of unknown cause 2 years earlier, which could be related to an Arteriovenous malformation

raw.rationale: The histopathological examination showing spindle cells with branching ectatic vasculature and strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1 supports the diagnosis of Hemangiopericytoma.

rejected.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
rejected.why: Lack of specific histopathological features and immunohistochemical profile

rejected.label: Cavernous angioma
rejected.why: Contrast-enhanced brain MRI suggested this, but histopathology did not support it

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Typical meningioma features such as desmin and EMA positivity were not found

rejected.label: Arteriovenous malformation
rejected.why: Imaging and histopathology did not demonstrate the characteristic vascular malformation
